core_obligations: Base change of quasi-separated morphisms is quasi-separated, giving the direct implication (proof lines 1434-1439).
Setup: each chart diagonal $\Delta_i : X_i \to X_i \times_{Y_i} X_i = Y_i \times_Y (X \times_Y X)$ is quasi-compact (proof lines 1439-1447).
Base change of an fpqc covering is an fpqc covering, so $\{Y_i \times_Y (X \times_Y X) \to X \times_Y X\}$ is an fpqc covering; each $\Delta_i$ is the base change of $\Delta$ (proof lines 1447-1451).
Conclude $\Delta$ is quasi-compact by fpqc descent of quasi-compactness, i.e., $f$ is quasi-separated (proof lines 1451-1460).
proof_roadmap: Handle the direct direction by base change.
Read quasi-separatedness as quasi-compactness of the diagonal on each chart.
Recognize the chart diagonals as base changes of $\Delta$ along an fpqc covering.
Descend with the quasi-compactness descent lemma.
difficulty_reason: The proof reduces quasi-separatedness of $f$ to quasi-compactness of the diagonal, observes each chart diagonal $\Delta_i$ is the base change of $\Delta$ along the fpqc covering $\{Y_i \times_Y (X \times_Y X) \to X \times_Y X\}$, and descends with the delivered fpqc descent of quasi-compactness.
